authoritative_clock_rule: For session-budget decisions, model-authored timestamps are never authoritative. Anchor the session to the GitHub server created_at timestamp of the first successful claim/resume/progress commit made by this run. After later checkpoint/result/claim commits, fetch that commit and use its GitHub server created_at timestamp to measure real elapsed wall-clock time. Do not estimate elapsed minutes from subjective effort, token/tool count, or timestamps invented in JSON payloads.
timestamp_write_rule: Whenever a protocol file requires claimed_at, heartbeat_at, reviewed_at, completed_at, released_at, or expires_at, use an available authoritative current-time source. Never knowingly write a timestamp later than the GitHub server created_at of the commit carrying it. If an exact authoritative current time is unavailable, do not use an estimated timestamp as evidence that the session reached a cutoff; continue useful work and let server commit timestamps govern session timing.
handoff_clock_gate_rule: A voluntary normal handoff before the GitHub-server elapsed time reaches productive_target_minutes is invalid while protocol-valid useful work remains. Before stopping for time budget, verify with GitHub server created_at timestamps that elapsed time from the run's anchor is at least handoff_start_minutes. If it is not, continue the current unit or immediately claim/resume the next eligible unit.
effective_lease_rule: For ChatGPT workers, use the shorter of this rolling_lease_minutes and any longer lease advertised by an active review plan or translation epoch. The rolling lease is intentionally long enough to span the productive target and normal handoff boundary so lease pressure must never cause an early handoff. Refresh only after durable checkpoint save when a refresh is actually needed.
released_claim_rule: A released claim is immediately takeover-eligible. The successor must atomically replace it using the current blob SHA, preserving the prior partial_result_path and other durable partial-result evidence before assigning a new claim_id.
fast_claim_rule: After the minimum routing reads required by WORKER_START.md, claim or resume useful work as one of the first meaningful repository mutations. Do not perform broad repository, glossary, branch-history, or public-source analysis before owning a work unit. If a claim race is lost, immediately try the next eligible same-priority unit.
partial_checkpoint_rule: Save a partial result after every checkpoint_every_decisions completed items or heartbeat_every_minutes, whichever comes first. A checkpoint is durability, not a stop condition: after saving, continue the same task or immediately select the next eligible unit while session budget remains.
productive_session_rule: Treat productive_target_minutes as the minimum voluntary-work target. While any protocol-valid useful work remains, do not voluntarily end before that target. Completing one unit, checkpoint, validation, stage, or small subtask is an immediate continuation trigger: re-read only the minimum live routing and claim/resume the next safe eligible unit at the same highest priority. Do not infer that the session budget is nearly exhausted from elapsed subjective effort; use the authoritative GitHub-server clock rule and configured minute thresholds only.
continuation_rule: When a unit completes before stop_new_batch_after_minutes, immediately re-read live routing and claim/resume the next eligible unit at the same highest priority. Never idle merely to wait for handoff_start_minutes. Do not stop after one completed unit if another safe eligible unit remains.
write_rejection_continuation_rule: If a required GitHub mutation is rejected before reaching the repository by a tool, policy, safety, transport, or connector layer, do not bypass that layer and do not treat the rejection as task completion or a voluntary session-end signal. Refetch live state/SHA and use another normal supported repository operation if available; otherwise immediately switch to another protocol-valid eligible unit/path and continue useful work. One or two rejected write attempts are not a voluntary handoff reason before handoff_start_minutes.
canonical_parallel_rule: During initial canonical hardening, domain research/hardening/testing is parallel across independent task branches and task-specific domain claims. blocking_maintenance blocks mass review/translation/UI work, not independent canonical-domain workers.
canonical_integration_rule: Live-main canonical integration, production Sync/no-op proof, and completion-state transitions are serialized through work/orchestration/maintenance_claim.json. Parallel domain workers must not publish canonical changes directly to main.
parallel_claim_fallback_rule: If another worker owns the non-expired primary maintenance claim during canonical_hardening, do not stop solely for that reason. Scan roadmap order for another dependency-satisfied parallel_eligible canonical task with an unclaimed/released/expired task-specific claim_path and claim exactly one such domain.
ready_for_integration_rule: A parallel domain worker whose substantive domain work is complete checkpoints its branch, sets that roadmap item to status=ready_for_integration and stage=ready_for_finalize with optimistic concurrency, then releases the domain claim. Other eligible domains may continue without waiting for integration.
final_sweep_dependency_rule: canonical-final-conflict-sweep is not parallel-eligible and must wait until all earlier substantive canonical domains are complete on live main.
maintenance_heartbeat_rule: A maintenance or domain lease refresh is valid only after NEW durable progress evidence has been persisted since the previous claim write. A time-only heartbeat that merely changes heartbeat_at/lease_expires_at is forbidden. Because rolling_lease_minutes spans the productive target and normal handoff boundary, this rule must never be used as a reason to hand off early.
maintenance_progress_evidence_rule: Every maintenance/domain claim refresh must record a changed progress_token plus progress_kind/progress_ref that identifies durable GitHub evidence, such as a new task-branch head, changed persistent task checkpoint, newly completed validation/sync run, or orchestration-stage transition. The same progress_token may never be used to extend a lease twice.
maintenance_no_progress_rule: If there is no new durable progress evidence, do not refresh the lease merely for time. Continue useful read-only/analysis/validation work while the existing lease is valid, or create a real durable checkpoint when appropriate. Lease timing alone is never a voluntary stop signal before handoff_start_minutes.
maintenance_finalizer_rule: The primary integration owner serially performs cleanup, safe integration onto live main, full validation, production Sync/no-op proof, spot checks, and completion transitions. Branch divergence is an integration concern, not a reason to restart domain inventory.
execution_backend_rule: Repository work is execution-backend independent. No external harness, plugin, shell, local container, MCP provider, or other backend is implicitly required. A failure of one backend is local to that capability and is not a task-level blocker while another repository read/write/execution path remains available.
backend_failure_fallback_rule: After a rate limit, EOF, DNS/network failure, unavailable shell/container, transient tool error, or rejected individual write, preserve the task and claim when valid, continue with available connected GitHub read/write capabilities, and use repository GitHub Actions/validation workflows for required execution evidence when the local runtime is unavailable.
backend_failure_handoff_rule: Do not release or end a worker solely because one execution backend failed. Do not bypass platform safety. Switch to available connected GitHub/repository paths or another eligible unit and keep working until the normal handoff boundary. Required acceptance tests may not be skipped when claiming completion.
session_end_rule: At handoff_start_minutes, stop starting broad new work, save the latest valid partial state, and hand off cleanly before session_minutes. If a small bounded step can safely complete inside the remaining budget, finish it first. Do not intentionally leave an active claim at session end.
throughput_rule: A worker must claim/resume another batch/unit until stop_new_batch_after_minutes whenever protocol-valid useful work remains. Prefer continuing from released/expired partial work over untouched work when both have similar priority. Completing one unit early is a trigger to continue, never a reason to end the worker.
